title: Expo: Fluid Futures
content: From micro-organisms and seaweed cultivation to wastewater treatment and ecological restoration: water connects life forms, technologies, infrastructures and communities. In Fluid Futures, artists explore these complex relationships and explore how people, technology and aquatic ecosystems can flourish together.

title: Actionperspectives through Citizen Science
content: The impact of citizen science is not always immediately apparent. Waag Futurelab investigated the opportunities that citizen science offers to residents, public authorities and research institutions. The publication Actionperspectives through Citizen Science sets out the key findings of the research.

title: What's beyond the ban?
content: Meta censored queer and feminist organisations earlier this year. Most of these accounts are now back thanks to the effort put in. However, this doesn’t mean that everything immediately returned to normal afterward. So, where do we stand now, and what are the next steps to be taken?

title: A month at Det Digit Art House: interview
content: Det Digit was one of the first digital artists in the Netherlands, working from a house in the woods near Knegsel, twenty minutes from one of Europe's largest technology manufacturing regions. Her last wish was that the house become a residency. Since 2024 it has been exactly that. This summer, in a residency run by Det Digit Art House together with Waag Futurelab, two artists spent a month there.

title: Guanyan Wu explores soy resist dye at Waag TextileLab
content: During her residency, Guanyan researched soy resist dye, a 400-year-old textile technique from Guizhou, China. Her work explored how this traditional craft knowledge can meet contemporary digital tools, opening up new ways to think about materials, technology, and craft today.

title: Join the discussion on art, culture and generative AI
content: On Sunday 6 September, the annual Paradiso Debate will take place, with Waag forming part of the editorial team this year. This year’s debate focuses on generative AI: what is the power and influence of the cultural and creative sector? Led by moderator Rosalie Dielesen, creators, administrators and politicians will engage in a discussion on this topic.
